std/alloc.evidence: Forge model/store and standard validation exercise owned allocation, collection ownership, and raw pointer helpers.

std/async.evidence: Forge scheduler and TCP server execute promises, runI32, TaskGroup, and async disposal; low-level handles are retained for runtime coverage.

std/bytes.evidence: Forge protocol and server paths build, slice, cursor, read, and write byte buffers.

std/collections.evidence: Forge store uses Map; the collection validation corpus exercises the complete collection family and iterators.

std/console.evidence: Forge server failure path and the standard validation corpus exercise console output.

std/core.evidence: Core interfaces and value types are compiler contracts; Forge uses Error, Iterable, and ParseIntegerError directly.

std/env.evidence: Forge selects its dynamic plugin and TCP port through lookup and checked u16 parsing.

std/ffi.evidence: Forge opens the configured system library, resolves strlen, and closes the handle.

std/fmt.evidence: Formatter and Display are compiler-facing contracts covered by syntax and standard-library validation.

std/fs.evidence: Forge writes, closes, stats, and removes a filesystem artifact.

std/io.evidence: IO ownership and writer APIs are covered by validation/io and runtime acceptance suites.

std/net.evidence: Forge serves TCP, resolves IPv4, binds UDP, sends metrics, and closes sockets.

std/path.evidence: Path ownership helpers are covered by the filesystem and standard-library acceptance suites.

std/process.evidence: Forge records process identity and spawns/waits for /usr/bin/true.

std/string.evidence: Forge server command dispatch uses owned string operations; Redis protocol validation covers UTF-8 and parsing.

std/sync.evidence: Forge executes atomics, mutex guards, channels, and task coordination.

std/testing.evidence: Test assertion exports are consumed by the TypeNative test runner corpus.

std/thread.evidence: Forge observes thread identity and yields during worker-process orchestration.

std/time.evidence: Instant and Duration are exercised by the runtime/time validation suites.
